label: Caprock Mesa: repeated cleaned_or_serviced on module with declining benefit
headline: Washing blocks B01 and B03 at Caprock Mesa now returns about 1-2% instead of the historical ~5%, with technicians confirming clean glass and re-washing to no effect — the remaining deficit is likely not soiling and warrants a module diagnostic before further wash spend on those blocks.
action: Commission a module-level diagnostic on B01 and B03 (IV-curve sampling plus EL or handheld IR on representative strings) paired with one controlled long-interval wash on B01 to separate irreversible optical/electrical loss from wash cadence, and fix the asset_id-versus-narrative mismatch in the wash work-order template before the next cycle.
reasoning: The late-period narratives contain the discriminating test H2 and H3 would have failed: on WO-2025-01057 the tech re-washed two rows specifically to rule out a rushed job and got the same ~1%, and on WO-2026-00620 he walked the block himself and recorded 'glass is clean' at ~1% recovery — so the residual deficit is not removable soiling and is not a copied phrase, it is an independent observation. WO-2025-00856 ('under 2% back, less than last round, panels looked clean') and WO-2025-00715 ('down on what it used to do') are two further techs independently reporting a decline relative to prior cycles on B03. H4 (site-wide reference drift) is weakened because in the same window WO-2025-00706 (B06) still returned 4% and WO-2025-00810 still returned ~5%, so the shortfall is block-specific rather than a uniform step in the measurement basis. H3 retains real force on the early figures — 'up close to 5% on the reference' is verbatim across WO-2024-00049, 00094, 00145, 00194, WO-2025-00238 and WO-2025-00810, and the narrative block disagrees with asset_id on WO-2024-00145, WO-2024-00194, WO-2025-00715 and WO-2025-00856 — so the 5%→1% magnitude is unreliable even though the direction is corroborated. The matched controls are inspections and torque sweeps, not washes, so they cannot rebut the finding, but they do show B01 has never had a module-level diagnostic (IR flights exist only for B02, B04, B06), which is exactly the gap to close.
contradicting: The early 5.0% values are boilerplate text repeated verbatim across WO-2024-00049, WO-2024-00094, WO-2024-00145, WO-2024-00194, WO-2025-00238 and WO-2025-00810, so the baseline is a template default rather than an independent measurement and the 2.6-point drop magnitude cannot be trusted. Narrative-stated block contradicts the asset_id field on WO-2024-00145, WO-2024-00194, WO-2025-00715 and WO-2025-00856, meaning the cluster may be mixing blocks. Two members (WO-2025-01007, WO-2026-00355) carry no benefit figure at all, and days-since-last-wash is not available, so the H2 cadence explanation is not formally excluded — WO-2025-01057 falls only 11 days after WO-2025-01007 on the same block.

population_detail.description: Module blocks B01 and B03 at Caprock Mesa, where post-wash recovery has fallen to ~1-2% with visually clean glass confirmed by the technician.
population_detail.basis: Distinct blocks named in the low-benefit late-period narratives (WO-2025-00715, WO-2025-00856 = B03; WO-2025-01057, WO-2026-00620 = B01). Module or MW counts per block are not derivable — installed_base is null.

hypotheses.statement: Block B01 (and possibly B03) modules have suffered an irreversible optical/electrical loss — abraded glass, AR-coating wear, cemented mineral soiling or module degradation — so washing now recovers only ~1-2% because the remaining deficit is not soiling.
predictions: Post-wash narratives in the late period should repeatedly state the glass/panels look clean while output remains low (already seen in WO-2025-01057, WO-2026-00620), and re-washing the same rows should not change the number.
The affected asset_ids should be a stable, small subset (B01/B03) while other blocks at Caprock Mesa still show ~4-5% wash benefit in the same months.

Downstream work orders on the same assets should escalate beyond cleaning: resolution codes shifting to ESCALATED / VENDOR-REFERRED / PART-REPL, IV-curve or EL inspection work orders, or warranty-claim entries after 2025-08.
Baseline (pre-wash) performance for those assets should be drifting down over successive cycles, not just the wash delta.
discriminating_evidence: A wash performed after an unusually long dry, dusty interval on B01 that still yields only ~1-2% — this rules out the 'less dirt to remove' explanation.
Independent module-level diagnostics (IV curve, EL, thermal) recorded on B01 work orders showing degradation, versus clean diagnostics.
Other blocks at the same site washed in the same week showing normal 4-5% recovery.

hypotheses.statement: The apparent decay is a wash-cadence and weather effect: late-period washes were performed at much shorter intervals (and/or after rain events), so less soiling had accumulated and the recoverable benefit was correspondingly smaller.
predictions: Days-since-previous-wash on the same block should be systematically shorter in the late window (e.g. 2025-08-30, 2025-09-11, 2025-10-17, 2025-10-28 are 12, 36 and 11 days apart) than in the 2024 window (~4-6 weeks).
Benefit_pct should correlate with the interval since the prior wash on the same asset, across all blocks and both periods, not just with calendar date.
Late-period work orders should carry fewer 'dust_or_soiling' environment tags or narratives noting light/no visible dust, and labor hours per wash should trend down if less scrubbing was needed.
Site-wide wash frequency (work orders per block per year) should be higher in 2025-2026 than in 2024.
discriminating_evidence: Regressing benefit_pct on days-since-last-wash: if interval explains the drop, the residual time trend disappears and H1/H3 lose support.
A long-interval late wash returning to ~5% benefit would confirm H2 and refute H1.
Presence of precipitation/rain-related environment tags or narratives immediately preceding low-benefit washes.

hypotheses.statement: The 'decay' is a logging artifact: early benefit figures are boilerplate '~5%' text copied between work orders (narratives all say B01 while asset_id fields say B01/B02/B03/B04), so the early mean is a template default rather than a measurement, and the 2.6-point drop across 13 records with 2 nulls is not a real efficacy trend.
predictions: Early-period benefit_pct should be almost perfectly quantised at exactly 5.0 with near-zero variance (5 of 5 in the sample), while late values are more varied (4, 2, 2, 1, 1) — a signature of a copied phrase, not independent measurement.

Narrative text strings should be near-duplicates across different wo_ids and different techs ('up close to 5% next clear day' repeated verbatim in WO-2024-00049/00094/00145/00194/2025-00238/2025-00810).

Narrative-stated block should disagree with the asset_id field in a substantial fraction of the cluster (already true for WO-2024-00145, 00194, 2025-00715, 2025-00856), meaning the cluster mixes assets.

Resolution_code should be inconsistent with the extracted action in several rows (PART-REPL, VENDOR-REFERRED, OTHER, ESCALATED all coded as cleaned_or_serviced), indicating loose data entry rather than a physical trend.
discriminating_evidence: Compare extracted benefit_pct against independent SCADA/production deltas for the same dates: if SCADA shows a real 5%→1% change, H3 fails; if SCADA deltas are flat, the trend is textual only.

Re-key the cluster on asset_id from the narrative rather than the asset_id field and re-run the early/late split — if the trend vanishes or moves to a different block, the cluster was an aggregation artifact.
Check whether the same boilerplate '~5%' phrasing appears at other sites in the same period, which would mark it as a corpus-wide template.

hypotheses.statement: The measurement reference has drifted — soiled, mis-calibrated or replaced reference cells / a changed SCADA baseline after mid-2025 — so post-wash gains are being computed against a degraded comparator and read lower even though actual cleaning recovery is unchanged.
predictions: The step down in reported benefit should be abrupt and site-wide (all blocks, all techs) around a single date rather than asset-specific; note the drop appears across TECH-0044, TECH-0131 and TECH-0236 alike.
There should be work orders around mid-2025 touching sensors, reference cells, pyranometers, met stations or SCADA/data-acquisition components at Caprock Mesa.
Narratives should shift in how benefit is sourced ('on the reference' in 2024 vs 'per SCADA' in WO-2025-00706), consistent with a changed measurement basis.
Blocks that are washed but never compared to the affected reference (e.g. handheld IV or inverter-level comparison) should still show ~5%.
discriminating_evidence: Existence and date of a reference-cell/sensor calibration or replacement work order that coincides with the benefit step change.
Whether the benefit drop is uniform across every block at the site (supports H4) or confined to B01/B03 (supports H1).
A wash whose benefit is quantified by an independent method on the same day as a reference-based figure, showing a systematic offset.

exposure_note: Priced at the cost model's inverter replacement rate. This population is not inverters, so treat the count as the reliable figure and this dollar value as indicative only.
